utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could we bring the witness -- wait. Wait a minute. Mr. Seric? Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. While the usher is bringing in the witness, I would like to introduce to you a former member of our team who has joined us today, our legal assistant, attorney at law, Mr. Danijel Gradac. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Welcome to this trial. You may sit down. Bring the witness, please. Mr. Stringer, before the witness comes in, could you inform us of how long you are going to take in your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's always difficult to predict. I expect to finish the cross-examination during the second session this morning. During the second hour and 15 minutes of proceedings. That's my goal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, I can hear you, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, yesterday when we broke, the witness was looking at B/C/S version of Exhibit PT 2 which had the yellow tabs on it and I'd ask that that be provided again to the witness so that we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just a few items remain on this document, Mr. Rajic. I'd ask the usher perhaps to assist us if he could get the English version of the transcript and I'm going to ask that a couple of pages be put on the ELMO as we do this. While that's being prepared, Mr. Rajic, let me try to bring you back to where we left off yesterday. This is the transcript of the meeting which you attended in Zagreb on the 27th of December, 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes. If this is an authentic document. You are referring to the document as an authentic one but I'd like to emphasise that it is a conditional situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Ultimately, sir, I think it will be the Trial Chamber's job to determine to what extent they find the document to be authentic based on the testimonies that come from a variety of witnesses, so I'm not going to ask you questions deliberately along those lines. I know you don't know how the transcript was prepared, for example. If I recall correctly, from your testimony yesterday, however, I believe you said that the statements that are attributed to you in this transcript appear to be an accurate reflection of what you said at this meeting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What I'd like to do now is to draw your attention to the part of the transcript in which Mr. Kostroman read into the record the minutes of the meeting that had taken place a few days earlier, in Tomislavgrad, on the 23rd of December, 1991. Okay?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And it's my understanding, sir, that you were among the people present in Tomislavgrad at this meeting on the 23rd of December; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, what I'll do is to first direct you to -- on your transcript, tab number 7. It would actually be the page right after tab 7. And for the English version, we are going to go to page 12 of the English version on the ELMO, please. Mr. Rajic, for you, I think this is -- and for the booth, 00850400. I'm sorry, 00850399, just the preceding page. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Maybe you could switch his television on to the video evidence and then you will be able to position the paper correctly. Okay. That appears to be pretty good.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, just for the benefit of all of us, Mr. Rajic, the minutes indicate that the session, this Tomislavgrad session was chaired by President Mate Boban and then what follows are the names of a number of people who took part in the discussion, and those include yourself -- your name is -- appears directly after the name of Mate Boban; is that correct, although it appears to be misspelled?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is a more extensive story about my family name. There have been a few versions but I know that I'm referred to in this particular case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if I could, Mr. Rajic, ask you just to turn to the next page, I believe, of your transcript and we'll go to the English version, page 13, B/C/S page 00850400. I want to ask you just a brief few questions about some of the items that are reflected in this -- in these minutes, which I think you should be finding at your tab 8. I'm looking at item number 2, which appears at the very top of the page in the English version, in which it is stated that, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna has once again confirmed the will of the entire Croatian people of Herceg-Bosna expressed on 18 November, 1991 in Grude. "Taking the historic decision to establish the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna which serves as a legal basis for the entry of these territories into the Republic of Croatia." So, sir, my question to you on that point is whether, in fact this is the case, that among the reasons for the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was to, in your view, or the view of your party, provide a legal basis for ultimately entering into the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I'd like to recall my statement made yesterday that these minutes, as far as I'm concerned, contain a great deal of flaws, both in linguistic and political terms. What is missing is more fine-tuning and nobody asked me whether this statement, should it prove to be true, will be the way it is. It leads us to a conclusion which basically is not correct. A decision made by the representatives of a people concerning the establishment of a temporary model of defence and common life under duress can be no legal basis whatsoever, particularly no legal basis for the entry into the territories of another state. I consider this to be an uncredible, an incredible statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's then move forward. I'm going to stip a couple of items; I'll come back to them. If I could ask you to go to your tab 10, English version page 17, and then for the booths, this is at page 00850405 of the B/C/S version. Mr. Rajic, isn't it true, as indicated here, that you signed these minutes, together with Mate Boban and Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what it says here, yes, but I cannot recall ever seeing a document that I signed. I cannot claim that I did not sign it, but that doesn't mean that signing it I could have noticed the differences that arise from punctuation marks and that lead to these differences. I may have omitted to notice this. But this is why I would like to draw this Tribunal's attention to the fact that the formulations and the wordings in these minutes are not always a faithful reflection of what we wanted to say and what we concluded. This doesn't apply just to these minutes. There have been similar occasions of this sort before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Isn't it also true, sir, that at no time during this meeting with President Tudjman did you express any reservation about the language or the statements that are being provided to him in these minutes? You never objected to any of this during your meeting with President Tudjman?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at this text closer, then you'll see that President Tudjman, through this -- these minutes, went through these minutes as a fact that he took note of. We did not go into it, and I think that it is about time for Their Honours to be submitted the statements I had made and not to be asked all the time to interpret what people thought at different points in time. If I'm allowed to do this, it will turn out, Mr. Prosecutor, that you have persistently been preventing me from sharing with Their Honours the thoughts and opinions that are quite different from those that go in favour of the Prosecutor's cause.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, I think that's a little unfair to the Prosecutor this morning, [indiscernible] yesterday because he specifically was asking you about your role at that meeting in relation to the minutes. There may have been other occasions where you feel you weren't allowed to speak because you were maybe going off the points, but I think this morning, the questions are directed to your own role, Mr. Rajic, but if you feel that Mr. Stringer is stopping you from answering, you can appeal to us. But it doesn't appear that way so far this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, let me if I --

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can assure you that I'll try to follow your instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Are you able to say yes or no? You did not object to the minutes as provided to President Tudjman in this meeting by Mr. Kostroman? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. The purpose -- a purpose of this meeting was for you, and other members of your delegation, to go to Zagreb, to provide President Tudjman with accurate information about the position and the activities of the HDZ party in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, inter alia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, if I could direct you to back up, Mr. Rajic, to tab number 8 of your version, English page 13, B/C/S page 00850400.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And now item number 3, and this goes a little bit to some of the things we discussed yesterday. In this item, it states that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna recognised, in the meeting in Tomislavgrad again, the full legitimacy of Dr. Franjo Tudjman as president of the Republic of Croatia and president of the Croatian Democratic Union to promote the interests of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, both among international factors and during interparty and inter-republic agreements on the establishment of the final borders of the Republic of Croatia. Now, Mr. Rajic, this item gives rise to two questions for me. The first is, again, isn't it true that President Tudjman was, in fact, the leader, the -- at the highest level, of both the HDZ in Croatia as well as the HDZ in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I fail to understand the substance of your question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You and other members of your delegation, on behalf of the HDZ of Bosnia provided to President Tudjman the authority to act on your behalf?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And this authority to act on --

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you did not allow me to finish my thought. In the talks in -- with the international community, because obviously we did not have access to this type of talks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So again, he was your interlocutor in respect of international -- the international community?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was authorised to represent the interests of Croats both in Bosnia and Herzegovina, also of Croats in Bosnia and Herzegovina, who were at that time living in a legally undefined territory. We were neither independent nor were we part of Yugoslavia; practically two-thirds of the territory had been occupied. And these facts determined our conduct and our demands.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And as such, then, you and the other leadership of the HDZ in Bosnia accepted his leadership and his instructions in carrying out the policies which he sought to undertake on your behalf?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't need that authority. Mr. Tudjman was president of a party, constituent part of which we were also. Let me emphasise, within the then existing state of Yugoslavia. I do not know how you men of law refer to this but my conclusion on the basis of this is that it was not necessary to introduce this definition of his but he's there, this is what it is, and I cannot change it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And his authority on your behalf extended as well to negotiations regarding an expansion of the borders of the Republic of Croatia to include areas of Herceg-Bosna, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not said anywhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, what does this mean, then, these last few words of item number 3, in which you authorise him to promote your interests on agreements on the establishment of the final borders of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, let me repeat it. The Republic of Croatia was then occupied, in fact more than two-thirds of its territory were occupied. There were offers made also in the course of some international meetings to make territorial concessions to Serbia or to Serbia's aspirations and along those lines, this is a statement and a declaration through which an attempt is made to help President Tudjman to be free to seek solution and not to be constrained in any way. This is why the Republic of Croatia is being mentioned and Bosnia and Herzegovina is not. Croatia had a great deal of difficulties in trying to establish its authority and to liberate its territories and some of these issues remained unresolved into this very day such as the issue of Prevlaka.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. But this is the situation, we have a delegation of leaders of the HDZ party who have come from Bosnia. We have a document in which the leadership of your delegation, the members of your delegation, have invested in President Tudjman authority to act on your behalf, including in respect of agreements, any agreements on the establishment of the final borders of the Republic of Croatia. Now, the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. fact that you and your group are giving him that authority strongly suggests to me that in fact what's being considered is a revision of the borders of Croatia which would encompass the territories whom you were reporting to represent, that is the territories of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not a correct interpretation of the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So if this document indicates that the leadership of the HDZ wanted to redraw or was providing President Tudjman with the authority on its behalf to redraw the boundaries of Croatia, to encompass, to include, the territory of Herceg-Bosna, that would be an incorrect statement, an incorrect interpretation of this document? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the incorrect interpretation. This is prejudging something that never was said explicitly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, you can set aside the transcript now; we are finished with it. We can take that off of the ELMO. I'm going to ask you some questions now about the Vance-Owen Peace Plan.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, now, you see, I was right. Therefore, I would plead with you to allow me to share with you three details that the Prosecutor avoided. I'd like to share with you quotes of what I had said at that meeting and I'd like to draw attention to the one and only relevant conclusion made at that meeting before we proceed with the questioning by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You may, but in a very concise way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I'll try to be brief. In a part of this text, when I contradict the opinion -- when I oppose the opinion that from Zagreb that we received an order for pursuing of the policy I said the following --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would, please, the witness tell us what part of the text he's quoting from?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, if I could assist, I could ask Mr. Rajic a few questions that would put us into the transcript, if that would assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: First of all, we have to know where this paragraph is, Witness. Maybe Mr. Usher could help.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have a few minutes to find exactly the section concerned, because I'm not allowed to make any markings on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, your statements in this, I believe, are found at tab 4, beginning at your tab 4.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And I believe that we are at 00850435, which in the English would be around page 36.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if I may, I've found it. So another opinion which the opponents of this political option, through Croat communities and further course which will be as the circumstances will permit, claim that the unconditional promise of annexing these areas to the Republic of Croatia may cause disagreements. We have never and no where said this expressly. We have said that it was our ideal and aspiration but that the institute of these communities needs to be broke out through some other form, political forms of the resolution of the crisis such as cantonisation, confederate Bosnia, or something third, that might surface. This is the end of it. On page 0050437, I am responding to the assertions of some of the members of the delegation that the policy has changed. And I say, "Also it is affirmed by some of our representatives, I mean the HDZ in Sarajevo, are claiming that in Zagreb, there has been a radical change out of the blue in the conduct of the party politics. That the concept of a sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina has been renounced suddenly and without any substantiated reason and that this creates confusion, disinformation and that this needs to be clarified." Now we come to the passage that the Prosecutor asked me about yesterday where I am interpreting the principles from the statement, declaration of the programme of our party of 1989, where we once again state our loyalty to the sovereign -- to sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina, until somebody else starts to attack it and eat into it and if somebody else does start doing that, then we know very well what our historical right is. And the third thing -- no, I can't find it but it's only one half of a sentence, but one can establish it and find where this text is. There were a series of objections to the leadership of the party headed by Mr. Kljujic, that they had failed to comply with the agreement of the 13th and the 20th of June, 1991, and that they did not go to talk at the same time in the same way with representatives of the Muslim and the representatives of the Serb people, and within that context, I say in front of everybody that one should have talked with both parties, not with Muslims only, and because some abhorred, the talks with the SDS, I said that some kind -- that any conversation was better than one death, and finally, I cannot really look through the whole document but I know, and it is my duty to say that, that the only relevant conclusion of that meeting was to continue talking with Serbs and with Muslims, and that the utmost needed to be done to avoid war and that every political agreement, any political agreement, that would result from the understanding of legitimate representatives of the three peoples should be accepted and as one can establish from this text, to this end, the Croat side appointed its responsible delegation to conduct these negotiations. Thank you very much, Your Honours, for giving me the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stringer. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. With your leave I would like to go back to one of the items that was just raised. I'll be very brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, can I ask you to turn to the first passage that you read which I believe is on your page ending with the number 00 -- 0435? English version page 35.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This is the passage in which you are talking, in which you said that we have never and nowhere expressly said that. We have said that it was our ideal and aspiration. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, what you're saying is that it was your ideal and aspiration to unify these areas within the Republic of Croatia. Isn't that what you're talking about here, taking into account the preceding paragraph?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, this is where I took a detour, because the whole world knows that a part of the people living outside the mother country always aspires to live with the mother country, if possible, and it does not cause some problems with a third party, so I'm talking about ideals. And ideals rarely come true in real life.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Secondly, in the next preceding paragraph, there is a reference to the meeting in Tomislavgrad on the 23rd. You refer to that meeting. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You say this: "We from Herceg-Bosna and the Bosanska Posavina claim that it is the meeting in Tomislavgrad on the 23rd of this month, showed that unequivocally, because out of more than 70 legitimate representatives of the Croatian people, only three or four of them expressed their reservations." Now, sir, what you're doing there is telling President Tudjman that the minutes of that Tomislavgrad meeting that he had already read to President Tudjman did, in fact, absolutely accurately reflect the will of the Croatian people of Herceg-Bosna, including yourself. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is difficult to answer with yes or no, if one does not read the introduction to the text which has been omitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The introduction to this says: "One of these theses of those who are not enthusiastic or oppose the concept of Croatian communities in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and who are saying that the establishment of these communities is not in line with the continuing policy of the -- with the constant policy of the Croat democratic union and Croatian interests in general." And then, the text that you read out ensues -- and which is very logical extension of that opinion. In point of fact, at the heart of arguments of some people was not what the world -- what the Croatian community will do but whether the Croatian -- Croat community Herceg-Bosna will threaten the leading position of the members of the party Presidency. Some of them thought that is party parallelism which is a completely incorrect interpretation and within this context, I justified a decision to establish the Croat community and its full support that it was granted at this meeting in Tomislavgrad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry. Could I ask a question while we are still here because I'm getting mixed signals from what the document appears to say and then what you, Mr. Rajic, say was actually happening. It's not a simple question. At the end of the meeting, was there any consensus that in the absence of a further invasion by Serb forces, that the ideal of a sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina would be maintained? Now, I know it's a double negative, so at the end of the meeting, in the absence of a further invasion by Serb forces, was it still the ideal of your party, your political party in Bosnia-Herzegovina, that the number one ideal would be a sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina, or was that a minority view?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is not what we argued about or at least not what we chiefly argued about, and there were some arguments, one can see that, from the discussion, because there were differences as to what one's attitude towards reality should be. Should one wait? Should one join the Muslim policy and follow that or opt for one's own way? So that was one of the chief issues concerning our differences, and in those meetings that you, Your Honour, asked about, voting was not a regular -- a customary procedure. And as regards our option, our ideal, whatever possibility came through, including a Serb attack, it invariably meant sovereign and independent Bosnia and Herzegovina, clearly well organised within as an organisation -- as a community of three constituent and equal peoples. And it is only in the condition, that is only as a possibility, we also mentioned those solutions which would be indispensable if, by force of arms of the aggressor, or with the consent of the international community, were it to be partitioned. Only then, only then we are mentioning a different solution. In all the other cases we are talking about the sovereign and independent Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, I recognise that the discussions all took place in the context of obviously a war situation, and what I'm basically trying to ask is in the absence of Serbian aggression, was it the aspiration even then of your party, not the party in Croatia, but your party in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I know they were sister parties. Was it the ideal that you would hope for a sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina with the conditions that all people were treated equally? Or was it at that time the position that the party was split on that and the majority were moving towards the aspiration of closer ties to the greater Croatia? I know all these discussions took place in the context of the fear of a further invasion, so obviously your views were coloured. And we see that. But what's coming across, and what Mr. Stringer is trying to put to you is that really the vast majority of your party had moved away from the original platform to the Croatian platform. When I say Croatian, I mean the Republic of Croatia platform, the greater Croatia. Is that true? Or what is your answer? I know it's not an easy question. That's really what Mr. Stringer has been spending three or four hours at.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I understand, Your Honour, the gist of your question. A vast majority of the political representatives of the Croat people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, who were by and large in the HDZ, never renounced, never relinquished their practical and the only useful objective, and that was the establishment of a democratic, equitable and sovereign Bosnia and Herzegovina. Because whatever -- every other solution we would have to stay in Yugoslavia under the Serb domination. And even when the referendum took place, when we objected we were not happy with the way the question was worded, because it did not provide the answer to an important question, of vital importance, and that is what is this state inside, what are the relations in it? We nevertheless swallowed that bitter pill, aware of the risk, brought about by the question which is taken to the referendum, but the expression, the independent and sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina, we put that in the first place, and it is common knowledge that at the invitation of the Croat Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but also at the recommendation, public recommendation of President Tudjman, the Croat people in Bosnia-Herzegovina came out, participated in the -- turned out at the referendum, 90 per cent of them, and there they voted for a sovereign and independent Bosnia-Herzegovina. I hope I have answered your question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I still want to know, Mr. Rajic, whether at the end of that meeting, you say there was no vote, but was there a consensus that you were moving further away from the original platform, if you like, of the HDZ when it first was elected in the open elections in 1990? Now we are a full year down the road. Was there now a movement away from the first aspirations and platform and what was discussed at Tomislavgrad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All misunderstandings or major misunderstandings were resolved during the -- in the course of the discussion, and we adopted this fundamental, perhaps the only relevant conclusion, at this meeting, by consensus, go to Bosnia-Herzegovina, live there as you cared and must, talk with both peoples, see what can be done to avoid war, accept any possibility of a peaceful solution that will satisfy the minimum Croatian national interests in Bosnia-Herzegovina, avoid war at all costs. These were talk, talk, talk, get away from war, get away from war. That is the only real conclusion. All the rest could be some side, sporadic conclusions, but not this one. And President Tudjman, indeed -- not only then, but he verily searched for micro millimetre areas where one could build peace and understanding. And these good instructions of the president, we tried to translate into life. And Mr. Kljujic, as the President of the party in Bosnia-Herzegovina, stopped Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. listening to what Izetbegovic was talking about. He was trying to see here what both Izetbegovic and Karadzic and our representatives of the political life in Bosnia were saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That's been very helpful. Thank you Mr. Rajic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, let's go back to one item that I hadn't intended to deal with but I think it may be helpful to all of us. If I could direct you, sir, to your tab 6? English version page 64, for the booth, 00850492. While we are going to that, sir, do you recall Stjepan Kljujic offered his resignation to President Tudjman at the conclusion of this meeting because of the criticism he received from other members of the delegation and President Tudjman at the meeting? Do you recall that he offered to resign?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please give me some time? I need to have a look at this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This would be the bottom third of the English version. Bottom third of the page.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've seen it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In response --

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In response to Judge Clark's questions you mentioned that Mr. Kljujic had failed to carry out instructions that he'd been given in the June 1991 meetings. I believe that was your testimony. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You are right that he had failed to do it with regard to that aspect of the conclusion, that talks should be conducted simultaneously with representatives of the Muslim and the Serb people because Mr. Kljujic was talking with the Muslims much more than with the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And we are talking about the conclusions he failed to carry out which had been issued by President Tudjman in the June 1991 meetings with him, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand you. Could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes. Yesterday, we looked at an exhibit that was marked IAC number 2. And that was a document which made reference to meetings and conclusions reached in meetings with President Tudjman in June of 1991. Do you recall that document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I think you testified that you were present at the meeting that took place on the 13th of June, 1991.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, when you say Kljujic didn't carry out conclusions or the instructions or he didn't implement conclusions, am I correct to understand that he wasn't carrying out the instructions he'd been given by President Tudjman in June of 1991?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. You didn't put it right. These were not President Tudjman's conclusions. It was what was agreed by those who were present at the meeting. All of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In any event, in any event, at this meeting in December of 1991, in Zagreb, Mr. Kljujic was criticised by certain members of your delegation, as well as by Dr. Tudjman, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some members of the delegation criticised Mr. Kljujic very seriously. I do not remember that President Tudjman addressed some criticism at Mr. Kljujic. I even believe he commended him for a number of things that he had done well. However, for the sake of a rounded off information, one needs to say that the criticism addressed at Mr. Kljujic was due to several reasons, apart from the fact that he had not talked with the Serbs. It was also --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, because I'm a bit conscious of the time and with the President's leave, I'd like to move beyond the reasons for the criticism and just to talk about the result of the criticism.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, I don't mean to cut you off but I'm more interested in the results, what resulted from the criticism, whatever the reasons for it. The result was that Mr. Kljujic offered his resignation during this meeting with President Tudjman; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He mentioned it as a possibility. However, the reason behind this offer was of a different nature. He was afraid that Mr. Boban might take over his office, and he would not suffer criticism, and that is why he tried a manoeuvre to formally offer a resignation to the -- both strengthen his position which was not in question. I mean that was only his impression.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: First of all, this is what he said, Stjepan Kljujic said. Directing you to the transcript. "Well, let me tell you regarding the policy here. It is not possible for the 7th dwarf to get up and make a ruckus about it. I did everything you told me to do. We cannot go on. You want Herceg-Bosna. You want Boban. Well, you're entitled to them, gentlemen. I resign. I'm always ready to resign, Mr. President." And then he goes on to make additional comments. Now, two questions. First of all, at the time of this meeting, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna had already been declared in its decision of 18 November, 1991, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, slightly over a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That was the decision that we looked at yesterday which -- in which you were one of the original signatories?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And as of 18 November, 1991, Mate Boban was the President of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was the presiding member of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: He was the highest ranking political office-holder in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But we cannot talk only about the political office, because political situation, because it is an association of citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, moving forward from this meeting in December into the early part of 1992, it's my understanding that Stjepan Kljujic finally did resign as president of the HDZ in BH, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. He submitted his resignation at Siroki Brijeg but again, he tried to regain it, to get it back later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: He was replaced by Mate Boban, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: He was replaced by Miljenko Brkic, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: My understanding that Mr. Brkic was, I believe, a university professor. He held the position for a relatively short period of time, and then was replaced by Mate Boban, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. But Mate Boban did not replace him. He was elected in a regular procedure, governed by the party statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So that in any event, we know that as of early 1992, for whatever reason, Stjepan Kljujic stepped out of position of president of the HDZ for BH.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not right away. For a while, he was the President in resignation, a resigning president.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it's time to move on to the Vance-Owen Peace Plan now. So we are finished with the transcript.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't need this any more?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, the Vance-Owen Peace Plan was unveiled in Geneva in the very early part of January, 1993, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It was unveiled to three parties, to the negotiations, the Bosnian Serbs, represented by Radovan Karadzic, the Bosnian Croats represented by Mate Boban and the Bosnian Muslims, represented by Alija Izetbegovic, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are correct facts but the nominations are not correct. There are no Bosnian Croats, nor Bosnian Serbs, nor no Bosnian Muslims. There are Croats, Serbs and Muslims from Bosnia-Herzegovina, living in Bosnia-Herzegovina, but the other facts, true.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I apologise if I -- I didn't mean any disrespect in the way that I described the three groups. The Vance-Owen Peace Plan --

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand it in any other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The Vance-Owen Peace Plan consisted of three components, all of which were inextricably bound up together. There was a list of constitutional principles. There was an agreement regarding the withdrawal of military forces and the implementation of a ceasefire. And then thirdly, the third component was the map. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, but all these facts were not revealed immediately. The political part of the agreement was the first, as the easiest one. The operational plan, the map, and the operational plan, followed only later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were you in Geneva taking part in any negotiations?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, neither in Geneva, nor anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Because I don't want to get bogged down into a debate or an argument about some of these questions which are public record. Would you agree with me, sir, if I were to suggest to you that prior to the 15th of January, 1993, Karadzic, Boban -- let me back up. I'll talk about the map first. The map that was proposed by Messrs. Vance and Owen would have divided Bosnia-Herzegovina into a number of provinces or cantons based generally along ethnic lines. Is that a correct statement?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd prefer to say as follows, to regulate Bosnia from within and organise it in ten provinces. That would be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And under the plan, the provinces numbered 3, 8 and 10 are provinces which would have been organised or regulated as Croat or Croatian cantons, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I think that there is a confusion. These are not cantons. In terms of the constitution, cantons are quite a different constitutional entity. We are talking about provinces. There were three for each people at the level of quality. In terms of quantity, things differed. And province number 10 was supposed to be given a special status and it consisted of the capitol and its surrounding areas, namely Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, well, if I could ask for the usher's assistance, Mr. President, we could put on the ELMO Exhibit 207.1, which is a new one, a new exhibit, I believe. It's just a map. And while we are doing that, Mr. Rajic, I was just -- the translation or the interpretation I received is that you indicated that province number 10 was to be given a special status and that it consisted of the capitol. I don't know whether that's your mistake or someone else's. Are you referring in fact to province number 7 as the one that would have had a special status?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I may have caused this confusion because I was talking to the tenth, the tenth remaining one and I was not referring to the numbers which were given to them but of course we are talking about province number 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And now the map is on the ELMO and we can get a general idea of the different colours. Would you agree with me, sir, that this appears to be an accurate depiction of the various provinces envisioned under the proposed Vance-Owen Peace Plan?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult, given the short time available, to say whether the map is faithful. Basically, it features the solutions, but to be able to make this confirmation, I would indeed need to study it in greater detail. It seems to me, however, that there are certain areas but it's very difficult to see all the details on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And I hope you'll accept my representation, I'm not trying to trap you. I don't think it's essential for our purposes that it be perfectly accurate to every detail. If you wish, you could take the map off the ELMO and look at it more closely. I would just like to get a general idea of whether this is a sufficiently accurate map.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's approximately true. Maybe even 100 per cent true. I can't really confirm. The structure is as it should be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, can you actually say that is the Vance-Owen map?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This is -- yes. I believe I can. I'm not anxious to make a firm representation as an advocate but I can say with confidence that this is the map. This is an exhibit, in fact, from a different case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So you can't actually say to this witness, here is the map that was proposed in the Vance-Owen Plan?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I can put a different exhibit to the witness, which would enable us to do that, which would be P239.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Wouldn't that be a better idea?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, it would. It just doesn't have the colours and so it's harder to work with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Give him both maps. Wouldn't that be the best thing and then we can all agree that it is the Vance-Owen map and then the comments will be directed towards that premise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Very well, Judge Clark, yes. With the usher's assistance, if we could provide the witness with Exhibit P239.1? It's already in evidence, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, while that's being organised, you're going to be shown a document that's already in evidence. It's a United Nations document that describes the negotiations and the events taking place in Geneva, also containing the different components of the proposed plan itself. And I believe the sixth -- the sixth piece of paper which you're now looking at is a map. It should be annex 3. Just to make sure we are looking at the same page because the map appears in different places here, could we go to the sixth piece of paper in this exhibit? Sixth piece of paper. Sixth page, starting from the beginning. That's it. Let's use that one. Yes. Mr. Rajic, as you look off to the right-hand side of that piece of paper, you'll see it says, "Annex number 3."

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see it, although this is a very poor copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I agree. Okay. Now, if -- are you able to -- again just all I want to do is try to get generally the contours of the different provinces, particularly 3, 8, and 10. Is it possible, sir, that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you could work comfortably with the coloured map, which would perhaps be easier to work with? Does it appear to correspond to the map that has just been provided to you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one of these maps, certain corridors can be seen around Brkco but I don't see the meaning of my verifying these maps because I was neither the author of them nor was I responsible for their implementation, et cetera. I don't know, I'm in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, you testified about an order that you issued on the 16th of January, 1993. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In your order, you describe certain events which you were ordering to take place in provinces 3, 8, and 10; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order, I haven't been describing this in the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You also ordered, sir, certain things to take place in provinces 1, 5, and 9, in your order of 16 January; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not just to them but to the ten of them, to all of them, to the whole of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All I want to do, sir, is to use the map so that we can specify, get a good idea of the location of the various provinces. Can we work with Exhibit P207.1 in order to do that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll use both. I apologise. I turned my microphone off. I'll be using both of them to be able to answer your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, is it break time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Bring in the witness, please. Yes, Mr. Stringer. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, we were looking at the maps that were proposed as part of the negotiations of the Vance-Owen Plan in Geneva. Now, I would like to direct your attention to the territory that falls within the proposed provinces number 8 and 10. If you could just look at those areas. First of all, let me just ask you this: Territory number 3, which is in the northern part of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that -- my understanding is it's part of a region that we call the Posavina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. But before that, Mr. Prosecutor, this map was not proposed. It was an adopted and signed by the representatives of the Muslim people.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We'll talk about that later, okay? But I'm going to ask you some questions before we get to that point, all right? I promise you we are going to have a full discussion about who signed and when. Okay? Province number 3, the Posavina, by this period of time, there was an entity that was called the Croatian community of the Posavina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The community was called Bosanska Posavina, but it was not an entity.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The provinces 8 and 10 that I now draw your attention to, it appears to me, sir, that in looking at this map, and the municipalities that fell within these two provinces, we are talking very substantially about the same territory that fell within the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and again we can talk about some exceptions, but would you agree with me, sir, that the territory covered by proposed provinces 8 and 10 are territories that correspond significantly to the same territories of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In geographic terms, approximately, but I don't see the relations between Herceg-Bosna and this plan. Is anybody implying that we decided about this plan? Or was it the international community that proposed it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sir, if you might just try to confine yourself to answering my questions, we'll get to the bottom of all this. I'm just asking you a simple question. The territory covered in provinces 8 and 10, does it appear to approximate the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna as it existed in January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in addition, under the terms of the plan as proposed at the beginning of January, these provinces were to be established along ethnic or national lines. Would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, primarily on this basis, but not only on this basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, so that to the extent that the Vance-Owen Plan was proposing the establishment of provinces based on ethnic or national affiliation, this was something that had previously been sought by the HDZ in Livno?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Isn't cantonisation or the establishment of provinces along ethnic lines the very thing that the HDZ tried to get on the ballot for the referendum that occurred in the November, 1990, multi-party elections? No, I'm sorry. Is it true that the HDZ tried to get on the referendum for independence, which occurred in late February, 1992, essentially the same thing that was being proposed here, the establishment of provinces along ethnic lines for each of the three constituent peoples?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is true is the following: The HDZ tried to insert into the referendum question this concept as well, but it failed. However, we never spoke about provinces because at that time, we were not even familiar with this as a political or a legal concept. We spoke about cantons, about a model which is known throughout the world, using the Swiss model.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And my only question, sir, is whether that proposal appeared to have resurfaced as part of the Vance-Owen proposal that was put forward in early January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It contains the most significant principle, which is the principle of a tripartite system of Bosnia-Herzegovina based on equal principles. The principle therefore is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. So then what we have in early January is a proposal which would essentially meet the need of the Croats for -- I'm looking for your words so that I say that correctly -- provinces along ethnic lines. Actually those are my words. What we find, then, in early January on the map that's proposed is something that is significantly similar to the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and which also envisions the establishment of provinces drawn along ethnic lines for the three constituent peoples?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, a majority of your question was put correctly. However, for the second or the third time, you are referring to a proposal. This is not a proposal. This is the document adopted and embraced by the representatives of Croats and Muslims. And the Serbs embraced it on condition that they be given an extension period to consult their so-called assembly. But the principle is the principle that we advocated: Each people in the same manner to be provided with a territory that represents the Bosnia-Herzegovina as a whole, as a unique state.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I promise you we'll get to the point about the extent to which these were agreed and ratified. I promise you we'll get to that. Before we do, however, let me just suggest it to you this way: When the Vance-Owen Peace Plan was first put forward in early January, then, it appears to me to have provided the Croats of Bosnia-Herzegovina and perhaps elsewhere with virtually everything that they had been advancing and advocating for the previous 18 months. Territory that substantially or significantly approximated the territory of Herceg-Bosna and a Bosnia-Herzegovina divided into three ethnic groupings along ethnic or national lines. That's my question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise to the learned friend. Your Honours, you will have noticed that I had no objections, but at this point in time, I believe that I need to intervene and say the following: Is Mr. Stringer here interpreting the Vance-Owen Plan and wants the witness to speculate on the Vance-Owen Plan? Because after all, the Vance-Owen Plan is a fact of history. It's part of history. Volumes of books were written about it. Everything is known about the plan. And if anybody were to -- able to witness about it, then it's Messrs. Vance and Owen and not the Prosecutor. I really wonder whether this is one of the duties of the Prosecutor and what he is trying to do with the witness. I was not objecting so far, although for three hours we have been talking about matters that are not substantial, such as the minutes et cetera. But now we have come to the crux of the matter and this is a demonstration of the fact that I was right in bringing these witnesses here, but I really fail to recognise the line of these questions. Is the Prosecutor trying to interpret his own -- is he trying to interpret the Vance-Owen Plan? But after all, this is a part of history. What is indeed his hope to get from the witness? Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the situation here is that the Prosecutor asked for several times a very specific question to this witness but this witness failed to answer this question. So as the last result, the Prosecutor put his case before this witness and asked this witness whether his characterisation is right or wrong. I think that's quite a logical questioning. If the witness believes that he does not agree with the Prosecutor, he can just say no. It's very simple. Witness, you may answer the question put forward by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Shall I ask it again?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be good.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could say counsel was cautioned yesterday about making comments about other evidence, specifically the transcripts that have been referred to. He did it again today and I object to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, I'll try to be more concise. When Vance-Owen was first put forward, when this map was first put forward, it basically provided you and the Croats of Herceg-Bosna with virtually everything that you wanted and had been working for for the previous 18 months. Territory along the lines of Herceg-Bosna and the partitioning of Bosnia-Herzegovina into three groupings based on ethnic or national lines. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is not. The most important thing was peace.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Boban on your behalf, and on behalf of the Croats, immediately signed all three parts of the plan, the constitutional principles, the arrangements for a ceasefire, and the map, correct? He immediately signed all parts of the plan.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot testify about that. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And in fact, in the months and weeks that followed, Mr. Boban continually and repeatedly signed different versions of the plan as they were proposed to the parties. He and your group were always in favour of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And all the other plans that addressed peace, before and after.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, as of the 15th, 16th of January, 1993, sir, Radovan Karadzic on behalf of one of the other parties, had signed only the constitutional principles, he had not signed the map, nor had he signed the proposals for implementation of the ceasefire. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the kind of information that the public had.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: As of 15th and 16th of January, 1993, Alija Izetbegovic had signed only the constitutional principles, he did not sign the map, nor did he sign the proposed agreement on implementation of a ceasefire. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not how it was represented. It was said that he had accepted the whole plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Where was that said?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the media, we were told that by the head of the Croat delegation from Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Boban, and others too. Whether it was -- it meant nothing more than initialing, I cannot say that. But the most important definitions, points of the plan, were accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Are you saying that you don't personally know whether that was the case or not, as of 15 January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not there personally but I had to accept the information that was brought to us by the legitimate representatives of the Croat people from Bosnia-Herzegovina who had attended those negotiations. That is natural.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That's an interesting point because we have to keep in mind that in January 1993 you were also the Minister of Defence for the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I don't understand why it should be interesting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You didn't consult with Mr. Izetbegovic as to his side, his version of the events that had occurred in Geneva, by mid-January?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic had other associates. He did not need me. He never called me. He never asked for anything. He never consulted with me. And he never informed me about anything. He behaved as the leader of the Muslims absolutely, not the -- not the leader of the state, from the Croat point of view, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The fact is, Mr. Rajic, you don't know whether or not Mr. Izetbegovic had agreed to the entirety of the Vance-Owen Plan by 15 January, 1993, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was informed about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Now, can we agree that by the 15th of January, the Serb side had not agreed to the Vance-Owen Peace Plan?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that. I do not know it, when they recognised it or something. What I can say is that when the media carried this information, that the two sides had accepted the agreement and the third had signed on certain conditions and that is how I learned about it. I didn't have any other sources of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So your sources of information were the media, and whatever Mr. Boban had told you, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Mr. Boban alone. Other members of the Croat delegation too, but needless to say, yes, most of it came from Mr. Boban.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Boras characterise the Geneva negotiations?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I saw him, whether I met him during one of those critical days that you are talking about. That is around the 15th, 16th of January. Later on, yes, we talked about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that the Serb side never agreed to the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Vance-Owen Plan?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It was --

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did but they had certain conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Which were put to the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina in the form of a referendum which they rejected. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Before that, the assembly, the parliament of the so-called Republika Srpska at the time met, discussed it and adopted conclusions and that was followed by the preparations for the referendum or, rather, the plebiscite, because it wasn't a referendum; it was a plebiscite. And only members of the Serb people participated in it, not all the citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The Serb side rejected the Vance-Owen Plan in a referendum that occurred in the spring of 1993, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You don't know other than what you read in the media and what others told you whether or to what extent the Muslim side had accepted the Vance-Owen Plan. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had information from the media and the delegation of the Croat people in those negotiations that Mr. Izetbegovic had, on behalf of the Muslim people, accepted the plan without reservation, and this is a fact -- rather, this is a belief that I've lived with ever since.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could you be wrong?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, it is human to err but I don't think I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The fact that the Serbs never agreed to the Vance-Owen Plan means that there was never a Vance-Owen agreement, correct? There was only negotiations between three parties.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It will be correct to say that all that this plan -- with all its details was not rounded off fully, was not completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And so that it never came into formal existence as an internationally recognised peace plan, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it couldn't, because the Serbs had rejected it and the Muslims renounced it later on, disowned it later on. So the will of the Croats did not suffice for its operationalisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, your statement, sir, that they renounced it later on, implies that they had fully accepted the agreement. Which is a fact that you, sir, don't know, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how I understood the information that reached me through different channels and I was -- and this fact made me happy, namely that at least these two peoples have found common tongue regarding the future of the state and their mutual relations. I had no reason not to trust all this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm going to put this to you, Mr. Rajic. I don't expect you to agree with me. The fact is Izetbegovic in the first half of January, 1993, signed only the constitutional principles. He rejected the map, sir, on the grounds that it would have the effect of rewarding the ethnic cleansing that had taken place up to that point in time. He also rejected the proposed plan on implementation of a ceasefire as of January, 1993. Karadzic also rejected the map. Karadzic also rejected the proposal on ceasefire. There was no agreement by either the Serbs or the Muslims to the proposed plan as of 15 January, 1993, sir. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not true. It cannot be true. Mr. Izetbegovic, with all the reservations, but he was primarily -- his reservations chiefly had to do with what the Serbs were about to get. I am not aware that there were some questions left open regarding the mutual demarcation between the Croats and the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think I'm just going to refer the Trial Chamber to Exhibit P239.1 on this point and try to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, what happens -- what happened in January, 1993, is that the Croats, Mate Boban and other members, Croats, in the HDZ, decided to unilaterally implement their own version of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, whether or not either of the other two sides agreed to it.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And if I could ask the usher to show -- we'll put P14 -- I'm sorry, P214, P215, P216. P216 is -- I think they are all in evidence. 214, 215, 216. Sir, the fact is that in Geneva, Mr. Boban signed all the agreement because he and the Croats found that it provided virtually everything they'd been working for and that when they saw the other two sides were not willing to sign at that time, decided to go forward and to implement what they understood as the terms of the agreement in the territories 3, 8, and 10, which were proposed as Croat territories in the Vance-Owen Plan. Isn't that true? Before you take the documents, if you could just focus on my question, give us an answer, and then we'll go into each of the documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we've been listening to one and the same question. I'm looking at my watch, for 17 or 18 minutes now, and to this same question, we have already heard the same answer during the 17 or 18 minutes. I believe that our learned friend is insisting on something to -- about what -- which he has already been given an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that the Prosecutor is moving to another subject, which is related to this one but indeed we have spent much time on that issue already. I hope you could move faster.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'll do my best, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, in your direct testimony, you spoke about Exhibits 214 and 215. Can we agree that 214 is an order issued by Jadranko Prlic on the 15th of January, 1993, which essentially is an attempt to bring about the subordination of Muslim armed forces to the HVO in Vance-Owen provinces 3, 8, and 10, with corresponding orders that would apply to the Muslim provinces?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm truly sorry, and I do not wish to complicate matters, but I really do not know how to respond to this form of cross-examination. The Prosecutor comes up with three claims more often than not opposed claims, in each one of them, and then wants me to answer with yes or no. I cannot do that. So may I be asked shorter and clearer questions, explicit questions? And then I will answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may try that, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, 214, is this a document signed by Jadranko Prlic dated 15 January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can we put the English version on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is what it looks like. There is the name and the signature of Jadranko Prlic but it is not an order, it is a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It's a decision bearing the number 01-I-32/93.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, we had this discussion before many times. What is the point of putting to a witness who is not a signatory to a document and may never have seen it before, a particular document. It's only when they are his own documents that there is any point putting them to him but we've got the point, that it is the Prosecution's case that the Vance-Owen Plan was not adopted and therefore should not have been acted upon. It is this witness's case that he has proceeded on the premise since January, 1993, that the plan -- that the -- all issues between territorial problems between the Croat entity in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Muslim entity in Bosnia-Herzegovina had been resolved. Now you are at diametrically opposite points. He disagrees with you. He doesn't accept that he could be wrong although to err is human. That he has acted sincerely under the premise that Mr. Izetbegovic was bound by the plan and you're proceeding on the other. So there really is no point in flogging a dead horse. He's not going to accept that these orders were unlawful. So we really ought to proceed. We take your point. We've got that, and I'm not criticising you but I think we better move into an area where we can make some progress. We are not going to make progress here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Clark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I should say that this witness is holding, appears to hold a sincerely held view, and at the end of the day, we've got to decide the factual basis and get down to the indictment, but I appreciate all the help but we are not going to progress.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, I'm reluctant to give my own characterisation, our own views on the sincerity of the witness while the witness is present. I think I can say that we are certainly not bound by his claims of sincerity. It's our position that what happened -- if I may put it to the Trial Chamber, this is where I'm going, and if you don't want to -- if the Trial Chamber thinks we should move often, then we can do it. A series of orders was issued in mid-January, 1993, by Mr. Prlic, by Mr. Stojic, also by Mr. Petkovic, who at the time was the Chief of Staff of the HVO. At the same time, on the 16th of January, this witness issued an order that was essentially identical to those being issued by the HVO, only this witness did so as the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It's our submission that this was all done as part of a political decision taken to implement the Vance-Owen Peace Plan even though it didn't exist. Now, -- and that as a result of this series of orders, issued by all of these people, including the witness, this resulted in armed conflict that occurred in a number of places which this Trial Chamber has heard about in the direct examination of this witness as well as other witnesses. So it's our submission that this is all taking place, knowingly, as part of a political decision to implement something that was not agreed, was not recognised internationally, and that it led to armed conflicts among the Muslims and the Croats. And that's what I propose to put to this witness and to examine him about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Well, I think we understand a lot of that but the issue now is you're saying that in was a deliberate employ to misinterpret the Vance-Owen Plan in order to start the conflict. Whereas the position that Mr. Rajic is coming from is that they believed that they were acting on foot of the Vance-Owen Plan. So perhaps you should put the question to him that he and others knowingly misinterpreted the position under the plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, who was present as part of the Croat delegation in Geneva in early January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Mr. Boban was there, Mr. Boras, and I know a gentleman whose first name was Jure. I don't know his last name. Mr. Boban's secretary, I believe. But they were the two most important persons, Mr. Boban and Mr. Boras. Perhaps Mr. Akmadzic was there too. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The agreement in front of you makes reference to the peace agreement in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Geneva agreements. The agreements reached and signed at the international conference of the former Yugoslavia. Sir, the fact is there were no agreements signed by anyone except Mr. Boban and that you, Mr. Prlic, Mr. Stojic, all knew that, and that all of you agreed to go forward with implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan whether or not it was agreed by any of the two parties.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I truly think I'm not an unintelligent person. I'm not an inexperienced person. And I do understand something about the legal terminology, but the way that the Prosecutor speaks, the way he's asking questions, is beyond me. I cannot keep up with him. So I must seek your help. You promised us a while ago that we would have short and clear questions. Once again, these are sentences as long as sausages which are very difficult to keep up with, to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer. First of all, I think you have to ask this witness whether there is agreement or not. That's a very simple question. We just want to know whether the witness believed that there is agreement or no agreement at all. Then later on, you could lead this witness step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, at the time that you wrote the -- your order of 16 January, is it your testimony that you believed there was an agreed, binding Vance-Owen Peace Plan, internationally recognised, and applicable to the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And once again, I cannot answer this question. You are involving me in a question with the word "all." I knew that not all had signed it and that is what my order says too. It says, I'm referring to the understanding or to the agreement reached in part, but I believed that an agreement had been reached between the Croats and Bosniaks or Muslims as they were officially called then, and that there were no matters of dispute between them. And I claim to this day that that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
