utterances.text: And as a result, you and other members on the Croat side decided to move forward to implement your understanding of those parts of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan that applied to Muslim and Croat territories?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I acted autonomously, as the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I did not work in accordance to our concept, as you called it, but deeply confident that I was implementing the peace plan in its entirety and it had nothing to do with the decisions of the HVO, independently.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you testified about the decision of Mr. Prlic. Is it your testimony, sir, that it's a coincidence that your order came one day after his?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is not a coincidence, but the basis underlying the two documents was the same and that was the Vance-Owen Peace Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At the time that you issued your order on the 16th of January, were you aware that Mr. Prlic had issued this order on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not know that he had undertaken anything; he or somebody else. Nor was I interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Prlic's order makes reference to a decision reached at a special meeting in Mostar on 15 January, 1993. Did you attend such a meeting?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I be present? It was a government body, a provisional government body of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and I wasn't its member.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Prlic ordered that this decision is to be implemented within Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. five days starting from the 15th of January, 1993. Do you see that? Item number 5.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we show the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honours. Once again the witness is requested to speculate. He said it loud and clear that he had nothing to do with Mr. Prlic's decision, that he was present at a meeting or that he knew anything about it and now the Prosecutor is asking him and all he can get from him is speculation. Plus the witness has already answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In this objection, I agree with you. You may proceed, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the question was whether Mr. Prlic's order set a deadline of five days. In my respectful submission it does not invite speculation. It just asks him to look at the document to tell us what it says. It's leading to my next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, let us hear -- let us hear what is the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit D1/90, please? Put the English on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, is this the order that you talked about in your direct testimony?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could I direct your attention, please, to item number 7? Page 2 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To avoid any confusion, Mr. Stringer said item 7 and in the B/C/S interpretation, we had 6, to avoid any misunderstanding between the witness and the learned friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Item number 7, the deadline for the implementation of this order is 20 January, 1993, by 2400 hours. Sir, is it a coincidence that you and Mr. Prlic both came up with the same deadline for implementation of this order?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not a coincidence. It is logical because the same information about the signing of the agreement, the need to enforce it and to do it within this period of time, I was following in exercising my duties and the HVO did the same. I was informed by Mr. Boban and other members of the delegation that within the five days, these activities have to be started and that the agreement, Mr. Boban, Mr. Izetbegovic, in talks with President Tudjman in Zagreb had been made. They stayed there for a while in order to reach an agreement as to how to operationalise this plan. So it's not a coincidence. It is in fact the foundation which has to do with the same facts, the same conclusions and decisions and what was done by the HVO, I do not know, and I cannot testify to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You consulted, then, with Mr. Boban in advance of issuing this order?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Didn't you just tell us that --

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say, sir, that I consulted with him. I was informed by Mr. Boban about the conclusions and then, following this information, I assessed and decided, in full autonomy, independent of any living soul in this world.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Boban told you that the terms of this arrangement needed to be implemented within five days?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not needed to be, but it was desired for them to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And on the basis of that information, then, you drafted up this order, which is defence Exhibit D1/90?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honours, my objection will be perhaps slightly longer but I will not spend too much of your time. Through this question, the Prosecutor is accusing the witness of drawing up a special plan for the enforcement of the Vance-Owen Plan, which allegedly had never existed. So I wonder what were Cyrus Vance and Lord Owen doing for four months because it's not logical for the Prosecution to first deny that something that existed and then somebody else be accused of having implemented this same thing. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, Mr. Seric. I believe that both parties have different views towards the Vance-Owen Plan in this aspect, but it's not an obstacle to prevent the Prosecutor to put his case to this witness. The Prosecutor is not accusing the witness at all. We have the order issued by the witness, and the Prosecutor is asking questions concerning this order. And this order has been used in the direct examination. Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I apologise. The Prosecutor, in this very hall, ten minutes ago, explained his view in which he had stated exactly what was now repeated by Mr. Seric. The learned friend quite clearly told us in this Trial Chamber that Vance-Owen Plan was on purpose misinterpreted, although they knew that it had neither been signed nor implemented to wage a war against the Muslims. This is what the learned friend said, and -- at least this is what my translation said. I object the following. At the very beginning, when Mr. Scott reacted when I said that if we are talking about politics, let us then see who is representing what line of policy and who is defending what I thought that this Tribunal is dealing with the Prosecution of war crimes. But as to the Vance-Owen Plan, I can assure you, Mr. President, that we will tender it in and if there is no other way out, we will pursue the invitation to bring Mr. Owen here. We tried it before. We received a negative answer. But as far as witness Rajic is concerned, to discuss his views and his deeds and things, I think deserves a slightly more lenient treatment. And particularly when it comes to the generally known facts. I apologise for this intervention, yet I'd like to thank you very much for allowing me to make this submission to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, we understand that there are different interpretations, different views concerning that agreement. It's quite natural for the two parties to disagree with each other. And here we are talking about the order issued by this witness himself. The witness has the full right to answer the questions put forward by the Prosecutor. The purpose of the witness to come here is to assist us to know the facts. That's a very simple question. Yes, Mr. Stringer. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think I forgot what the question was. I'll start over again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I think you were asking him about the state of his knowledge when he issued the order, and I would like you to ask this witness whether he saw any copy of the signatures to the plan and what documents he had in front of him that he relied upon when issuing the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The question is that on the basis of that information, then you drafted up this order, which is Defence Exhibit D1/90.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, did you have any documents in your possession on which you relied in order to know of the status or the -- status of the Vance-Owen Plan as of the time you issued this order on 16 January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upon return from Geneva, the delegation, both the Croat and part of the Muslim, spent sometime in Zagreb. I don't know exactly how long they had stayed there. Mr. Boban informed me of the decision made in Zagreb. In fact, he called me together with Mr. Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting you there. The question was about documents and Judge Clark specifically asked this question. Did you have documents in front of you which you studied to learn about the Vance-Owen Plan as of the 16th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was an announcement made by the international conference, peace conference in Geneva, and it contained all the most important elements of the plan. Of course without the maps. But everything else was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So are you telling us, sir, that on the 16th of January, you were aware that the maps had not been agreed?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't consider this to be important at all. I knew that they would be continued, that the detail to drafting in the field would be continued. The most important thing was the halting of war, establishment of peace, and common action of both Croats and Muslims, and this was my motive and this is what I would do once again today without thinking twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I see that in your order you make reference specifically to partly signed agreements. Those are your words.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. These are my words, and I am referring to the agreement made between these two peoples and the initialing by the third people, by the Serbs. Their conditional agreement by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And again, just so we are clear, the maps were not agreed as of the 16th of January, and you knew that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what you are claiming but I'm saying this is not true. The agreement had been reached but I did not have it in my hand, as far as the maps are concerned, and I didn't consider this to be that important for the order that I gave.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You then issued an order directing units of the ABiH, the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, to subordinate themselves to the HVO command in provinces 3, 8, and 10, under Vance-Owen, and you're telling us, sir, that you did that without being fully knowledgeable about the status of the agreements on maps?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, it is with great regret that I must say that you are putting words into my mouth. You, on purpose, skipped over the first item of this order where all units of the Croatian Defence Council are ordered to be placed under the command of the main staff of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. If we are to be fair and correct, let us proceed item by item, as far as this order is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You issued everything in this order, including the order that all armies disarm, and you did so without being fully knowledgeable about the status of the agreement on maps. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. Where does it say that I ordered the disarming of the armies? This is not said anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You ordered the subordination. Is that a word that we can use?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a misinterpretation, on purpose, of this word. To be subordinated, to be placed under somebody's command in military sense, means to be under the command of a specific level of military command and it does not imply either disarming nor any coercion whatsoever. It implies the recognition of the command of the staff or whatever is the particular military body concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You testified that you spoke with Mr. Boban before you issued this order. Did you speak with other leaders on the Croat side before you issued this order?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that moment in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you speak with Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said before that I never talked to Alija Izetbegovic about these issues because he was not willing to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So on this day, as the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, you issued an order that in part directed units of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina to be placed under the command of the main staff of the HVO, in Vance-Owen provinces 3, 8, and 10, and you did so without even consulting the President of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct. You are again referring only to one part of the order. I ordered everybody concerned to do so, and I told you that I could not consult with Mr. Izetbegovic. I was not important enough for him at that time. Very often he even refused to talk to Mr. Boban. This is why very often, it was necessary for Mr. Tudjman, President Tudjman, to talk to him so that Mr. Izetbegovic was able to talk to the adequate authority, and I hope you understand this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You were Minister of Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and you felt no obligation to even attempt to discuss this with President Izetbegovic before you issued this order?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said before, it was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The question was whether you attempted to do so.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said it before, sir, Mr. Boban informed me that in the presence of Mr. Izetbegovic, he was talking about it. Was I supposed to split hair to show a lack of trust into this authority? This is not what I would expect from you, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Where were you when you wrote this order?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So it says Sarajevo. So that's a misrepresentation, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not a misrepresentation. We agreed that regardless from where I'll be active, I will always use the capital of the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina and that all official documents will have the city of Sarajevo as the place issued. And this is something that was universally recognised by both the leadership of the Muslims and the Croats. This is not a misrepresentation. This is the result of an agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The fact is, sir, that when you issued this order, you were acting in your capacity as a Croat political leader and a spokesman for the HVO and not in your capacity as the Minister of Defence for Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what you claim, but yesterday I said that this is not true and I'd like to repeat this statement of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that you were still a spokesman for the HVO at the time that you issued this order?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you put it in very formal terms, then you can insist on that. But I could not make any decisions that had to do with my nomination or relief of my duty. This was done by other people like anywhere else in the world. In practical terms and following my conviction and my ethical values, I acted in my capacity of the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, on behalf and in the function of this state in the function of peace and all its citizens. All interpretations that go Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. beyond this are not fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The result of this order that you issued was not peace. In fact, it was armed conflict. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very dangerous misinterpretation, Mr. Prosecutor. This has nothing to do with the reality. And I'm offended. You're accusing me here. And I did not come here to be accused of anything. I have come here as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Isn't it true that, as a result of your order as well as others issued by Mr. Prlic and others, resulted in armed conflicts in Busovaca and in Gornji Vakuf when attempts were made on the 20th of January to implement the order that you and the others had issued?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to this question. I submit to you that this is another misinterpretation of what the witness is trying to say, and I object to this line of questioning because the Prosecutor has entered a sort of personal relationship with the witness which is neither professionally acceptable nor is it fair. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At any rate, in his questions, he includes speculations and is trying to lead the witness to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm allowed to ask leading questions on cross-examination, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And I don't believe I'm acting in a way that would suggest any personal judgements on my part. And so I respectfully disagree with what my learned friend Mr. Seric said. I do believe that this is legitimate cross-examination based on the direct testimony of this witness, however -- and I propose to proceed, although I can inform the Trial Chamber that I am reaching the latter stages of my outline on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we understand where you are aiming at at this point but you have to put your question another way so that you do not prejudge the results of the answer by this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, did armed conflicts between the Muslims and the Croats take place in Busovaca on the 20th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that there were conflicts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: There were also conflicts, very severe conflicts, between the two groups that occurred in Gornji Vakuf at the same time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was before. I think that was somewhere in October, 1992. I went there in order to extinguish that fire together with a delegation. There were some minor provocations that took place there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Isn't it true that these conflicts in Gornji Vakuf and Busovaca resulted from HVO attempts to implement your order and the order of Prlic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And that these attempts were made right on time, in accordance with the deadline set by you and Mr. Prlic of 20 January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true either.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that that's the conclusion that was reached by the international community who were present in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure what conclusions you are referring to, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Isn't it true that the international community present concluded that the hostilities that occurred in Gornji Vakuf and Busovaca resulted from attempts at unilateral implementation of these parts of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be possible that some representatives of the international institutions in Bosnia and Herzegovina characterised these conflicts in that manner but they are equally wrong, just like your submission.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe it's time for a recess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How long are you going to take for your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If I could just have a brief moment to look through --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if you need another ten minutes, we could continue to sit, but...

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I think I need more than ten minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, once again I tried to avoid the word "privilege." It is quite clear as to what was the time I used for my direct. The Prosecutor already has overstepped this period. Yesterday, he told me that he would try to reduce the breaks. He already had had four breaks; so did I. But I would indeed appreciate your equal treatment in those matters. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, I understand that during the cross-examination, it is very difficult to ask some questions from this witness. But it is indeed that we spend too much time on the Vance-Owen Plan which we know that the two parties hold different views. So I hope you could finish your cross-examination within 15 minutes after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'll do my best, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Bring in the witness, please, Mr. Usher. Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, at the time of the break, we were discussing the order that you issued on 16th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At the time, perhaps the same day or shortly thereafter, did you explain to the media the reasons why you had issued that order? Do you recall making any statements on television?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember. I did -- I gave statements to several media, both local and of a broader significance, and I believe I was also in a TV programme called Slikom na Sliku, picture against picture, on Croatian television.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time I'd like to show a video clip. It lasts about 90 seconds, perhaps a little longer but it's quite short. It's the programme that the witness has just described. I think that transcripts have been distributed already, or it's our request that that be done. This Exhibit number 905 is the videotape and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It may assist the witness as well, if we could give -- if there is an extra copy. It's in both languages, so... If I could ask at this time the people in the booth if we could perhaps dim the lights just a bit and run the video clip, Exhibit 905?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Still under the command of the HVO although they belong to the Sarajevo province. In the Siroki Brijeg is Mr. Bozo Rajic spokesman for the HVO. Mr. Rajic, good evening. Good evening. Why did you opt for this decision? It is known already that the situation and the attempt of extremist groups of Muslims to take away territory which historically belongs to the Croatian people, which they succeeded in defending from the aggression and which in the most recent times at the Geneva negotiations was internationally verified as the Croatian ethnic rights in Bosnia-Herzegovina. In view of the fierce battles, especially during the last two or three days that have been waged, in which the Muslim extremists have tried to destroy the resistance of the HVO first in Gornji Vakuf and elsewhere, it was necessary to undertake further measures to protect Croatian ethnic living space and the rights of all citizens who live on the territory."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is the first time that we see this tape. Even though my learned friend has given us the transcript, but now I see here three TV centres; the HTV, TVB and H, and in Cyrillic, ST. And I would like to know what the source of this tape -- where this tape came from, because I have never yet seen three television stations in one. That is on the screen. We had HTV, TVB and H, and ST, which stands for Serbian television. In Cyrillic, the last letter cannot be seen because of the ICTY logo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that the witness has answered that question. Maybe, Mr. Stringer, you could ask that question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, is this you appearing and speaking on the videotape that we just saw?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is me. But this was edited. You have taken only a part of it, and I'd be happier if the Chamber could see the authentic recording of the Croatian television in total. This is only a fragment and it is an abuse. And, yes, it is I who is in this programme. There is no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we've given the Trial Chamber what we have. This was found on a compile that we have that has many, many different things on it. I'm happy to let the witness give a fuller explanation but I think that there are some questions based on what's been said here that we would like to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, you were introduced as both the Minister of Defence in the cabinet of Bosnia-Herzegovina and also spokesman for the HVO. My question, sir, in which capacity were you acting when you said that the decision was the result of an attempt of extremist groups to take territory historically belonging to the Croatian people?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to this question, mostly because the witness has said, with regard to this video clip, that it has been edited and therefore the quote cannot be based on this video clip, as it is not authentic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seric, I believe this is only part of that programme, and what we need is only this part. I don't think the question asked by the Prosecution is not irrelevant. It just asks the witness that in what capacity the witness made that statement, after the witness admitted that he was the very person on that videotape. Mr. Stringer, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In Rajic, this was my question. In what capacity were you acting when you said these things? Minister of Defence for Bosnia-Herzegovina or spokesman for the HVO?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I once again am asking you kindly in the best of faith, do not ask me twofold questions. You say here that I introduce myself as the Minister of Defence in the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the spokesman for the HVO, which is not true. That is the presenter -- in the studio said that. I have nothing to do with it. I was there in the role which I had, the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, I said that you were introduced. I didn't say that you introduced yourself.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I understood that you said that I had introduced myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, I think that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the witness has answered the question already. So could we skip this question?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So getting back to my question, the original question is, in what capacity were you acting, Minister of Defence or HVO spokesman?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this question was asked and answered ten times ago and now again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I've never got an answer to this question, Mr. President. The debate has been about who introduced him in these capacities. I've never gotten an answer to the question itself in what capacity was he acting?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Line 21 to 23 of the transcript. Read it. Lines 21, 22, 23. And it says, "I appeared there as the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina." And it was all explained nicely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We also believe that the witness answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, let me suggest to you that in fact you were acting as an HVO propaganda man putting out the HVO view, and its own interpretation of the Vance-Owen Plan, as an excuse for the hostilities that were taking place in these areas.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question is put in the form of an affirmation, even though it lacks any foundation in facts. How could I, that same day, issue an order and already know about the facts of a conflict which it produced, as you are saying? That is nonsense. And secondly, I do not want to comment on a fragment of what I said, and I suggest, as the best possible solution, to take my statement in total from the Croatian television and then you will know what exactly I said, what the presenter said, and this whole issue. Otherwise, you are planting on me a fragment and I'm quite confident that it is edited, that it was edited.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Are you denying that you said these words that we just saw?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that this was put together, edited, that I'm confident about that, and I spoke at much greater length and with much more explanations than what you just showed us. And that is a serious difference. And I did not participate there as a propagandist as you called me and that is an ugly name of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The words that you said -- I'll ask the question again -- the words which we heard, are they your words, sir?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was edited, words cut out and put together. When you show me the whole tape, the whole reporting, then I will answer your questions. Until then, I have nothing else to say to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Rajic. You must answer questions, if Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you can. Did you say the words that were spoken on that short piece of tape? I accept what you say that it's not the whole programme. But did you actually say those words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As they are represented here, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I can help the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But this is a very important explanation. I'm not interfering with anything, but the sentences that -- the sentences are formed and that is what the witness is objecting to. The language. Because if some words are mixed up, taken out, put together, then the sentences are wrong. And that is what the witness is objecting. Because I understood the witness very well. I don't know how this is being interpreted. I do not know, but I believe I'm really now intervening in the best of faith.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We want to hear what the witness is going to tell us, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The witness answered categorically, no, they are not his words so we know what his answer is. They are not his words.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm prepared to move forward, Mr. President, in the time I've been given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, in your direct examination, I'm going to go forward now a couple of months into the month of April, 1993. And my learned Mr. Krsnik showed you an exhibit, it's marked P274. And it was a news service report indicating that an ultimatum type of statement had been given by the HVO in April, which, if I can generalise, fell roughly within the same terms as the January documents we've described, talked about, subordination, et cetera, within certain of the cantons. I can show you the article. Perhaps that's the best way. I'm just trying to speed along. P274. At the same time, we could give the witness P275. Mr. Rajic, my notes indicate that P274 is an article which you said was not an accurate statement, that it was some result of a Serb intelligence or news service which you did not believe was a credible one. P274.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, but for the Croatian text?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I need P274, please. Can he look at P274?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, I don't know that P274 exists in the Croatian language -- that's it. This is a Borba article? Mr. Rajic, sorry for the confusion. The single question was, my notes indicate that in respect of this article you said that this was patently incorrect, that the suggestion of an April 15th, 1993 deadline was nonsense.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And what is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Whether that's -- whether my understanding of your testimony is correct.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only up to a point. I said that this was a pamphlet, the propaganda of the greater Serbian machine, a lie, because the name of Mr. Izetbegovic is mentioned here separately as a person to whom the ultimatum had already been sent and I never saw that in any document. So it -- so it absolutely makes so sense to comment on this further. It is disgusting. It disgusts me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Exhibit P275 now, please. We have this one in your language, Mr. Rajic. It's an article, I believe, from Slobodna Dalmacija. You can put the front page in English on the ELMO. As you read that article, Mr. Rajic, I'm going to ask you to focus your attention on the part that quotes from a statement, a six-part statement, which as indicated here was signed by Mate Boban. If you could put page 2 of the English version on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were is Slobodna Dalmacija published, if you know?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, yes, I do know. In Split, in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And this article in its first paragraph makes reference to a session, a Saturday session, of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't hear the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The beginning of the article makes reference to a session of the HVO and a document announced by the press department of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Do you see that at the beginning of the article?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Is this the press department -- were you a part of this press department? Or is this a different office?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I don't believe you can't tell apart these two offices, or is it you are deliberately trying to confuse them? I told you that at that time, and until July, 1993, I was the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I had no function or ties with the Croat Defence Council, be it its military or its civilian part.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Moving ahead in the article to the six-point items, item number 2 indicates all armed forces of the HVO and police of HZ HB, and the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which originates from outside the provinces shall have to identify themselves and leave such provinces within three days. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The next item appears to be a reference to the provinces that we've been discussing under the Vance-Owen Plan, HVO units in provinces 1, 5, 9 will be placed under the command of the Bosnian army main staff, and at the same time, Bosnian army units in Vance-Owen provinces 3, 8 and 10 be placed under the command of the main staff HVO.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor, but I just do not know why you are reading this. I know what this is about. Why don't you ask me that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Next item, main staff of both armies to set up a joint command no later than 15 April, 1993. See that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this statement, these six points?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is no statement. This is no official document. It's a draft. It's a proposal, which Mr. Mate Boban sent to Mr. Izetbegovic to be signed by him, if he goes along with it. And you are showing me an incomplete document as a document on which I'm supposed to pass my judgement, and this, Mr. Prosecutor, is but a draft, but a proposal. That is how I know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you know about --

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about it as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you know about this draft at the time, early April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. We all knew about it. It was in the media, like this one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, skipping down two paragraphs after item number 6, in the events the statement is not signed by the heads of the Muslim delegation, in provinces 3, 8 and 10. The HVO of the HZ HB has decided to apply the provisions of the peace plan, whereby each national armed force will have to withdraw to its domicile province.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, that the Muslim delegations in those provinces did not sign and did not agree to the implementation of this draft?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do I have to do with this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm simply asking you if you know whether Muslim delegations referred to here ever agreed to this draft. That's my simply -- my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object, Your Honours. And I almost gave up after I saw Judge Clark react, because the witness is invited to speculate, to tell us what he thinks about what somebody else thought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no. I don't think so. The question was asked, simply asking you if you know whether Muslim delegations referred to here ever agreed to this draft. Witness, put aside this document. Just tell us whether you know or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that is a completely different matter and now I understand you fully. I do not know if the Muslim political leadership went along with this, but I don't think they signed this draft at long last, at the end of it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And as a result, sir, isn't it true that HVO units in central Bosnia, as well as in the Jablanica area, attacked Muslim villages beginning on the 16th of April, 1993, in places such as Ahmici, Loncari, Gacice in central Bosnia, as well as in the Busovaca and Kiseljak municipalities?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true. Conflicts did take place there but they had nothing to do with the document that you are talking about. Their relationship, their roots is much deeper and broader.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So it's your testimony, sir, that there is no relationship between the timing of the armed conflicts that occurred in mid-April, 1993, and this draft statement that was proposed by Mr. Boban?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I put it to you that on the basis of that, that nobody was authorised by this proposal to take whatever steps. If somebody did something on his own, then it has nothing to do with this draft and its nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sir, if, on the military side, within the military chain of command of the HVO, steps were taken to proceed after April 15th, militarily, you would not necessarily have been privy to or consulted in that decision, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, answering questions during these -- during the previous two days, I already said that my position as the Minister of Defence was necessary, that both sides needed it, but that my true terms of reference, my true jurisdiction over the units of both sides were fictitious. They simply did not exist. They did not ask me, nor did they authorise me, as I have repeatedly said already.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. One last question on this. The author of this article, Veso Vegar, is this the person who was your assistant when you were the HVO spokesman?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes but Mr. Vegar is a journalist by profession. I do not know if he's writing this in one or his other capacity. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Because in fact, as a journalist for Slobodna Dalmacija in April of 1993, he was also your successor in the information, the office which you held within the HVO?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I took no decisions about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna had something called a Narodni List; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The Narodni List is the official publication of all of the decisions of the government of the HVO of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All important decisions are published there. I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could be shown Exhibit P578.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, I have to warn you that your time is up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This is my last -- this is the last document and there will be one question and I'll be finished in two minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't have a translation of this. It's a document that we found last night after yesterday's testimony. We can put it on the ELMO. It's very short. I think we can easily work with it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, I want to direct your attention to the decision that's numbered 0312. First of all, I should ask, does this appear to be the publication from the Narodni List from Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Does this appear to be the decision relieving you of your position as the information or -- in your office that you held within the HVO?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then, the following decision, number 0313, is that the decision in which Veso Vegar is appointed to succeed you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, going back to the decision relieving you of your position, could you read for us paragraph number 1? It's at the very top of the second column.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could you read it out loud so that we can get an interpretation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Bozo Rajic graduate economist of Kupres is being relieved of his duty of assistant head of the defence department of the Croat Defence Council of the Croat community of Herceg-Bosna for information, propaganda activities."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That was in fact your job, wasn't it, Mr. Rajic, information, propaganda activities, the job that you carried out on behalf of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is what it says here, the word "propaganda" was used. I think this was the proofreader's mistake, because I never did, nor did I want to be involved in propaganda. My activity was of information and policy matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination? Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'll put a few brief questions to you so that we can explain it to Their Honours, which were put to you in the course of the cross-examination but you couldn't sufficiently expand on them. First, let us start with the tape. Upon the question by Judge Clark, who asked you whether these were your words that were on the tape --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, he answered that. It doesn't need clarification. He said that they were not his words. So we don't need any clarification. You only re-examine when you need to clarify something. It is clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. No, Your Honour. I apologise. With your permission, I hear what the man is saying and I can see the interpretation. I'll put him a question to answer what he wants, because it was not allowed to him to answer what he understood under the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. word "edited", or montage or doctored tape. We come from different backgrounds, from different cultures, from different punctuation marks, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, I understood what he said. He said that this tape had been edited, words had been taken out, words had been edited. He suggested it was not a genuine tape and they were not his words. What further explanation does he need to give us?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in that case, this is then really superfluous but this is not how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Well, the issue is how the Bench understands it and I think I posed the question in the context of what Mr. Stringer had asked and what his previous replies -- and I asked him to give me a definitive answer and he said they are not his words. And he explained previously why they are not his words. I mean, if in fact, a tape is ultimately found which proves that he's right or disproves what he says, that's a matter that we'll have to take on board in relation to the overall view of the evidence. But really, he made it quite clear. He was unequivocal, if I understand him right. Do you think he genuinely, in fairness, needs another opportunity? Yes do, but I think Mr. Rajic was quite unequivocal about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I can go along with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, are you familiar with the authors of the Vance-Owen Plan, with the persons who participated in its drafting, and whether, on the 18th of May, 1993, it was a subject of a discussion in Medjugorje?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All peace plans, from the Cutilheiro Plan to the Dayton Plan, are the result of an effort and the assistance by the international community and its authorised representatives over there. This plan too, with all the proposals and counterproposals, made by the three parties in Bosnia and Herzegovina is primarily indeed the result of international efforts. As such, it could succeed, and only as such. At the meeting in Medjugorje, we discussed models, the most efficient means for this plan to be brought into life after its being halted and stifled by the Muslim side. I myself was there, and I listened to the talks about it held between Lord Owen, Thorwald Stoltenberg, Mr. Tudjman, Izetbegovic more than others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were you also present or did you personally hear what was the opinion by Mr. Alija Izetbegovic? Did at that meeting Mr. Izetbegovic say to Mr. Owen and to the representatives of the international community that he did not want to sign the plan?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Objection, that's a leading question, Mr. President. I object to the leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, you have to put your question another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you hear, and were you personally present, at the discussions of Mr. Alija Izetbegovic with Lord Owen, Stoltenberg and other representatives of the international community?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could hear what was going on in the course of the plenary session, when the diversion of political and -- when they split into political and military talks, I no longer could follow the discussions because I went to pay a visit to the prisoners in the Heliodrom camp. However, I know it for sure that Mr. Izetbegovic is a very subtle politician whom I personally respect, who never gave explicit answers as opposed to me who am always giving explicit answers. I know that he never rejected it. He always left the door open and thus gave false hopes to many people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was there any discussion held in -- at Medjugorje between Lord Owen and the delegations and were the Muslims and the Croats asked whether they adopt the plan?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding of that meeting is that the plan was not the point of dispute but that rather certain details had to be defined and that the technique and the order of moves need to be determined to implement the plan in its part which referred to Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was the meeting convened for the sake of its implementation or for the sake of holding the discussion about it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the meeting was based on -- convened on the hope to reach a number of objectives. One of the objectives was to enforce what was agreed in Geneva but the prime objective was to halt the hostilities in the field between the units of the Croat and the Muslim peoples, and perhaps the third important objective, as I saw it, was the intention by the international community's representatives to once again establish and strengthen, with good views ahead of cooperation between Muslims and Croats in all its facets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did this eventually take place? Finally?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Fortunately in an important part of it, it did happen. Not in every aspect but in most of it, at least on a temporary basis. But policies went along their own courses afterwards, and again, we faced major difficulties and victims and casualties until Washington and the Dayton Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did the Washington Agreement, as far as the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna is concerned, get its recognition and a possible confederation with the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think in my answer, I have to make a distinction between two concepts, the Croat community or, rather, the Croat Republic of Herceg-Bosna was not recognised by the international community in a manner in which states are usually being recognised, nor had any one of us, the Croats, ever asked for that. But it was recognised as a legal and legitimate institution of the Croat people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, which emerged in a war situation and all its legal acts were recognised, apart from those which could be in contradiction to international law, while in the new community of the federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is until in the federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, common provisions are adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What about confederation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The confederation was an addition to the initial agreement, which envisaged an association of peoples, that is an association of the confederation of Bosnia-Herzegovina with the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we think that we would suggest that the Washington Agreement of March, 1994 and subsequent modifications of it are beyond the scope of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We believe so. Mr. Krsnik, skip this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I put this question as a logical continuation of all the Prosecutor's questions. Of course I'll skip it. It was not my intention anyhow to continue with the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, the meeting held on the 27th of December, 1991, in Zagreb, you were questioned, cross-examined, by the Prosecutor for hours with regard to this meeting. Did anybody at this meeting ask you, warn you, or let you know that the deliberations were taped?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did anyone personally give you the minutes of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was any other participant at that meeting given the minutes of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, nobody ever got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Had, by any chance, anybody got it, could you have any knowledge of this?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, why did Mr. Kljujic submit his resignation at Siroki Brijeg, if you have any knowledge of that? And for what period of time he continued to perform his function after resignation and for how long a period of time did somebody else perform his function? In other words, how long did it take until Mr. Boban came to this post?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hope that I've remembered all your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I apologise. You are right. I apologise. But I'm glancing at the clock.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very briefly, the President of our party, Mr. Kljujic, handed in his resignation because of the fierce criticism he was exposed to, given the -- his passive attitude with regard to the defence issues. Then because of his non-critical subjugation to the political will of Mr. Izetbegovic and the SDA. Then because of the criticism concerning bad personnel decisions and through his decision to hand in resignation, I personally, sincerely believe, he tried to prevent, to intercept if you want, a decision that he be withdrawn from this position. But for these reasons, not for other reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I apologise. You ever reminded me of another question. Did anybody force him to do so?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And which body is it that appoints the President?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a rule, it was the assembly, the sabor of the party. However a provision of the statute stipulates that during the sessions of the sabor, the executive board can also do that. I still owe you the answer to the second question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw Mr. Kljujic performing his duties for another period of time, perhaps a month. He was -- he continued to perform the duties of president-in-resignation. Perhaps somewhere from February to April. Later on, Professor Dr. Miljenko Brkic was appointed to this position, and Mr. Boban was elected president of the party somewhere in mid-December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: After the siege of Sarajevo, did the party HDZ have any communications with its representatives and was there anyone representing the HDZ in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me remind you that the activities of the party were frozen in the course of the war. There were simply no conditions for its activities. In Sarajevo, there were still some officials of the party who participated in the authorities through the HDZ paper, but their number was shrinking by the day because of the very adverse conditions there. Therefore this type of communication that you refer to in your question could not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell us for how long were the activities of the party frozen, from when until when, if you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we had a two stage procedure. The activities of the party were revived, first in those territories of Bosnia-Herzegovina where the clashes stopped, i.e., in the federation, and only after Dayton, it was fully re-established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe I have no further questions. Thank you, Mr. Rajic, for your patience.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you. I do not have any questions. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any questions from Judges?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I have two questions. And I don't want to take up much time because I'm aware that I have posed a number of questions during the proceedings and that I know that my colleague Judge Diarra has a number of questions. Mr. Rajic, am I correct in saying that at the meeting in Siroki Brijeg, when you talked of the resignation of Mr. Kljujic, that either during the dinner or shortly after he became gravely ill and had to go to hospital?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is ridiculous. Kljujic made it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: My next question, Mr. Rajic, is on a totally different matter. At the meeting in Siroki Brijeg with heads of, or representatives of the international community, you told us that you had left at some stage to go and visit the camps. And do I understand your evidence correctly, and I've made a note of this, to say that you visited the camp and I think the camp shocked you, Heliodrom shocked you, and you saw men of a certain age. Does that mean that you only saw elderly men there or men of only a particular age?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there and I suppose I did say I was shocked, because it is a very painful expression that you are left with when you see a large number of people confined to a very small space, whom I saw there were only adult men, that is, men turned of age, between 18 and 65 maybe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And is it your belief, Mr. Rajic, that the camp actually closed down on the 18th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the camp wasn't closed down that same day; it was impossible. But I'm confident that the Medjugorje decisions brought about their event you'll closure and that that never happened again. At least those that were on the Croat side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rajic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Judge Diarra, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is paradoxical that I have the same concern like my colleague, but in a slightly different sense. Mr. Rajic, your visit to the camp, to the Heliodrom camp, according to you was a shocking experience on the 18th of May, 1993. But did you have any information about those who were responsible, who ran that camp? Did you -- were you aware of any sanctions or did you contribute to the sanctions that would be taken in the face of that tragedy which shocked you, which disturbed you so much, which upset you so much?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am a freedom-loving man, and my encounter with something that is called a prison or a camp could not but produce very profound emotions in me and that is why I said, and in that sense, that I said that I felt terrible. At that meeting in Medjugorje, they wanted to solve the problem and they did solve it in a manner of speaking and it was measures -- it was Lord Owen, Mr. Stoltenberg, Mr. Tudjman, Izetbegovic and Boban. I had no authority over anything else, apart from what had been vested in me but I was left with the impression that the assessment of the reason for the conflicts between the Croats and the Muslims was shared by both sides, and I don't want to quantify it but that was the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. qualification for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You answered only one of the questions. I agree that perhaps you had no authority over this but my question was whether you were aware of the identity of those who caused this tragedy. Do you know -- did you know who could do that, who did that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My second question was when Mr. Stringer spoke about Bosnian Muslims, Bosnian Serbs and Bosnian Croats, you corrected him. You said that there were no Bosnian Muslims or Bosnian Serbs or Croats, that they were merely Muslims, Serbs and Croats from Bosnia, and I'd like to understand your reaction. According to the culture that I come from, the nationality means belonging to a common being. So you're saying that there is no Bosniak -- there are no Bosnian nationality there are merely Serbs from Bosnia which belong to the Serbian ethnicity and Croats to the Croatian and Muslims? I don't know. Will you please explain it to me? I did not understand your reaction at the time.

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I shall be very happy to do so, Your Honour, and I will explain why I reacted. I approach this matter from the legalistic point of view. The constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina as the supreme legal act of a state, those three peoples are officially called as I said, Muslims, Croats, and Serbs, without any prefixes or suffixes. You may have noted that throughout I spoke about Muslims, and that is also a legalistic attitude. To me they were Muslims. That is what they called themselves and whilst it was prescribed by the constitution. After the following -- following the establishment of the federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1994, the Muslims changed their ethnic name and renamed themselves as Bosniaks. I respect that fact and ever since that has been the only way in which I address them. Why I reacted in the way I did, I will tell you that too. Certain international representatives in Bosnia-Herzegovina now and then are unable to make this fine distinction, and I take their possible mistakes or slips in good faith. But in Bosnia-Herzegovina, there was a man, Austrian administrator, Benjamin Kallay who in the early 20th century arrived to us by the Austrian government to establish a new nation. And that is that theory about the Bosnians -- Bosniaks of three faiths, as the denial of the existence of three peoples, and that is why I reacted because it would mean an abuse of the right of each one of these peoples to call itself as it feels like calling itself. Only in accordance with its ethnic sentiment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judges' questions? I see none. Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, on the issue of the camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, you indicated to both Judge Clark and Judge Diarra that you had no subsequent knowledge about the Heliodrom camp after it was closed in May of 1993, and that you didn't know who was responsible for the camps. This is my question. Aren't you aware, sir, and didn't you say publicly in September of 1993 that we had to put a larger number of people in certain places than the capacities allowed? In every camp, of course, certain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I -- if a document is quoted, may the witness be acquainted with the document? May he be given it? And read it? Because we already have very bad experience with our three witnesses so far. I always insist, when a document is quoted, that it must be shown to the witness so that the gentleman can read it and know what it is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, you have to understand that there are some questions out of Judges' questions. It's not cross-examination again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So that you have to keep your question very simple, very concise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I am trying to do that, Mr. President, by simply asking him whether he said something that has been attributed to him about the camps in September of 1993. And if I could just ask to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Certain outrages occurred that are not covered by either a political mandate or a political order. We did not want that nor is it our intention to cover it up. Today, no one in the world can conceal everything. The places I'm skipping down, the places where the Muslim soldiers are imprisoned probably do not meet --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will you slow down, please. We do not have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- police places where the Muslim soldiers are imprisoned probably do not meet the standards of the international standards of the law of warfare and humanitarian law. Then you go on to stress that Herceg-Bosna has committed itself to bringing those into conformity with international humanitarian law. Now, I can put an article in front of you or my question at the moment is simply whether you refer -- making public statements about the camps, these statements, in September of 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you only tell me, Mr. Prosecutor, where was this published?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Rajic, did you say that? And then, if you didn't say it, what difference does it make where it was published?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not know, Your Honour. I meant to say that I did not remember, and perhaps the information about the place of publication would have refreshed my memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would propose to as quickly as possible put this in front of the witness and we have copies for distribution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I believe the defence has already been provided with this, Exhibit P606.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, what I will do for you is, on my clean copy, I will highlight the publication, the date of publication, and the part of the article which is on the second page, which I want you to refer to. I'm going to have to place it on the ELMO. It's in English only. Sir, the publication is the Vecernj List, 19th of September, 1993, interview with Bozo Rajic, director of the Herceg-Bosna news agency, former defence Minister of Bosnia-Herzegovina, written by Zdenko Duka in Zagreb. Now, do you recall giving an interview to Zdenko Duka of the Vecernj List in September of 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not, but it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Does it refresh your memory as to whether in such an interview you would have made the statements being attributed to you by this reporter, Zdenko Duka?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not particularly. Not in anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sir, I read you a part of this article. My question to you is whether you made public statements on behalf of Herceg-Bosna about the camps. Do you recall making any public statements about the camps in September of 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, you and I suppose this is your last question, and you are asking it in the same way. In September, 1993, I was completely outside any political system, outside any system of government, or any individual offices. I am a citizen, a free man, holding the office of the manager of a news agency, and I could only speak in my own name and in no other way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, the question is very simple. Do you recall making any public statements about camps in September of 1993? If you don't remember -- if you don't remember, just say no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, I said that I did not remember, but I'm not quite sure. It is possible that I did give this interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, I'll just put this to you one last time and then I think I will withdraw, to simply say to you, sir, did you say, in such an interview, "That a problem arose with space, we had to put a larger number of people in certain places than the capacities allowed, and every camp, of course, certain outrages occur that are not covered either by a political mandate or political order. We did not want that?" Skipping down, "The places where the Muslim soldiers are imprisoned probably do not meet the standards of the international standards of the law of warfare and humanitarian law." Now, sir, did you say that in September of 1993? Are these your words, given to anyone in any capacity, official or personal?

utterances.speaker: BOZO RAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that I did not know, but I do not know if we are speaking about camps retroactively as a fact that was, and that confuses me, and even I really cannot answer in any other way except that I just do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much, Witness, for coming here to help us by giving your evidence. We all wish you good luck in the future. The usher will show you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. May I ask you for a minute of your time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes. You will have to be very short.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have said one minute. Before I leave this courtroom, I wish to thank you, Your Honours, for enabling me to provide as complete answers as possible. I'm leaving this courtroom with a twofold impression. One is a positive one, the one that every man is bound to feel when he has done what his conscience bid him to do. And my second impression is that perhaps I have contributed a little in your search, in your pursuit of justice, and I also thank you, Mr. Prosecutor, although I disagree with the manner of your cross-examination, but you have also helped me to do what I came to do. I thank you, counsel for the Defence, because you have helped me to acquire a very useful experience, which perhaps will be of use to other potential witnesses from Bosnia-Herzegovina, to respond and come to help this Court. Your Honours, it was indeed a privilege. Thank you once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may go now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, Mr. Scott. We are under the pressure of the time because the next sitting will start in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm sorry for that and I apologise for trying the Court's patience but really one minute or less. We just simply would like to be advised by Defence counsel what the line up after this witness is both for tomorrow and for next week, because with all respect, since the Defence case started, the order and the names of the witnesses have changed several times rather dramatically. We would like to know who the definite next four or five witnesses are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, of course, I could not say on behalf of the Defence counsel but we were provided with lists. I think if there is no further notice, we will call the witness according to that list. Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honours. I have informed my learned friends about everything in time, about every single change, about every second, but perhaps Mr. Scott raised this matter yesterday. We received a submission. I do not know if you received it as well, concerning the next two witnesses, asking that they do not be examined. I do not know if you have received that because we are all awaiting your ruling about this. And we have already responded today to the application by the Prosecution. And I believe that was the Prosecutor's question, if I understood him right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, there is what I want to say at this moment. We have received this motion filed by the Prosecution yesterday, and we haven't seen the response from the Defence counsel. Since time is very limited, we believe that those witnesses have been in order already. We are going to hear from both parties tomorrow morning for about 20 minutes. I hope that both parties will express their view directly to this Trial Chamber tomorrow morning before you call the next witness. And at this moment, we have to leave this courtroom immediately. I would like to offer our apologies to the Presiding Judge for the next Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. case using this courtroom for this delay. We will rise until tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: be reconvened on Friday the 12th day of April, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
